question.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

$$
-\frac{2}{5}x+y=-3
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5}x+y & =-3 \\ (-1)\cdot (-\frac{2}{5}x+y) & =(-1)\cdot (-3) \\ \frac{2}{5}x-y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}x-y & =3 \\ 5\cdot (\frac{2}{5}x-y) & =5\cdot (3) \\ 2x-5y & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is 

$$
2x-5y=15.
$$
